adds.title: United Nations General Assembly document 2008 on sexual orientation and gender identity
adds.summary: On 18 December 2008 Cabo Verde joined 65 other states in supporting a UN General Assembly statement reaffirming that human rights apply equally regardless of sexual orientation and gender identity, expressing concern over violence, harassment, discrimination, exclusion, stigmatization and prejudice, condemning killings, torture, arbitrary arrest and deprivation of economic, social and cultural rights including the right to health, and urging all states to promote and protect the human rights of all persons regardless of sexual orientation and gender identity and to end criminal penalties on that basis.

adds.title: 2025 Joint Declaration proposed by Spain in favor of LGBTQ rights
adds.summary: On 28 June 2025 Cabo Verde joined a 15-state foreign-ministers joint commitment rejecting violence, criminalization, stigmatization and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, supporting eradication of transphobic harassment, promoting diversity and anti-discrimination policies and socio-labour inclusion especially for trans persons, calling for repeal of and refusal to introduce laws punishing sexual orientation and gender identity, demanding an end to criminal prosecution including imprisonment and death penalty and to conversion practices targeting sexual orientation and gender identity, and committing public authorities to implement effective LGBTIQ+ equality under international human rights standards.
